From: Lauren Caldwell <lauren@greengrid.ai>

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: SLA carveout request (GreenGrid AI)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We went to the product team and they are ready to move our real-time LLM inference to Redwood Dedicated, but we have a few hard constraints that we need to formalize in the contract before procurement will sign. High level:

- Production use case: inference for customer-facing recommendations and moderation in a live streaming pipeline (latency-sensitive).
- Desired commitments: sustained 180 QPS (inference requests per second) with the ability to burst to 260 QPS for up to 10 minutes, p95 inference latency <= 120ms, and minimal preemption during business hours (PST 06:00–22:00).
- Queueing behavior: requests tagged as "critical" (payment and moderation) must be routed with higher priority and not sit behind large batch jobs.

We understand these are atypical asks; GreenGrid is prepared to sign a 12-month reserved GPU commitment and discuss associated premium. I attached a brief requirements PDF with our expected traffic shape and a sample 48-hour QPS trace.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can (1) offer a temporary SLA addendum that guarantees the above headroom and queueing carveout while we ramp, and (2) what telemetry you need from our side to validate the carveout? Procurement and our security team will need specifics on the carveout language.

Appreciate the quick turn here—this is a priority for our Q2 launch.

Best,

Lauren Caldwell
Head of ML Ops, GreenGrid AI
lauren@greengrid.ai

Attachment: GreenGrid_sla_requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 312 KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.in>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.in>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: SLA carveout request (GreenGrid AI)

Hi Lauren—

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. Happy to take this on. A few clarifying questions so we can scope an addendum that engineering and legal will accept:

1) Traffic breakdown: of the 180 steady-state QPS, how much is "critical" traffic (payment/moderation)? Percentage and typical request size (avg tokens).
2) Burst profile: you mentioned bursts up to 260 QPS for up to 10 minutes. Are bursts expected more than twice per day, or is this a rare event during launches?
3) Failure mode tolerance: for the "critical" tag, are you asking for absolute zero preemption, or a preemption window (we usually allow brief preemption for rolling maintenance)?
4) Data/security: will requests contain PII or regulated data that impacts routing to specific regions?

Internally I'm looping in Karthik (product) to propose a concrete runtime carveout and Marissa (sales/finance) to align on the reserved commitment and pricing. From a process perspective, we can offer a temporary SLA addendum for the ramp period (30–90 days) with explicit telemetry gates; if the production traffic matches the profile we agree on, we can bake this into the annual contract.

Can you share a 48–72 hour traffic sample in CSV (timestamp,QPS,avg_tokens,tag) and call out which requests must be "critical"? That will help us size the queue priority and any KV cache reservations.

Thanks—will follow up after Karthik reviews.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Jordan / Marissa—

I reviewed Lauren's requirements and have sketched a pragmatic addendum we can propose. Key points below; I recommend we offer this as a temporary 60-day operational carveout while GreenGrid ramps, with explicit telemetry windows and credit mechanics if we miss the agreed headroom.

- Reserved throughput: guarantee 180 QPS sustained per dedicated pool, measured at the ingress gateway.
- Burst allowance: allow bursts to 260 QPS for up to 10 consecutive minutes, up to 4 times per 24-hour period. Bursts beyond that will be best-effort and subject to throttling.
- Queue priority: implement a "critical" priority lane (logical priority at the router) that routes critical-tagged requests ahead of batch jobs. Critical lane will be limited to 30% of total pool concurrency to avoid starvation of other tenants.
- Preemption/maintenance: during the carveout window (PST 06:00–22:00) we will not preempt critical-lane requests for rolling maintenance; emergency maintenance retains a 3-minute grace window for in-flight KV state reconciliation.
- Incident credits: if we fail the guaranteed sustained throughput for more than a 10-minute window during business hours, GreenGrid will receive a usage credit equal to 1 day of reserved capacity prorated to their monthly commitment.

Operational asks from GreenGrid to validate the carveout: one 72-hour sample CSV (timestamp,QPS,avg_tokens,critical_pct), and a tag mapping for which API calls must be treated as critical. Also confirm whether the traffic is routed from a single region (we prefer US-west) or multiple regions.

I've attached a short draft addendum with the specific SLO language and metrics we will expose in Redwood Console. It includes suggested monitoring dashboards (p50/p95, concurrency, queued-request depth) and the DocuSign stub fields we need for legal.

Thoughts? I tried to balance protection for GreenGrid while keeping our runtime ops simple and enforceable.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
